messages:
Alex (Sales): Heads-up — NovaSys procurement returned the vendor risk review and circled BCP/DR. They want a short, copy-paste block for: RTO/RPO, backup cadence, failover steps, SLA history, and DR test evidence. Can SRE + Legal craft something we can drop into their questionnaire? :pray:

Priya (Solutions Eng): I can assemble. One quick Q: they checked a box for "RTO ≤ 1 hour". Do we ever commit to that as a standard? Also clarify whether they want hosted vs Private backup control details.

Sam (SRE): Short answer: we don't promise 1-hour RTO for Hosted. TL;DR by offering:
- Hosted API: run for high availability with automated routing, but no contractual RTO/RPO. Typical recovery from infra incidents is measured in hours and varies by incident.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): covered by uptime SLAs (Standard 99.9% / Premium 99.95%). Operational recovery targets for full-environment failover are generally in the ~2-4 hour range depending on topology and warm-standby configuration.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed recovery; RTO/RPO are defined during onboarding and in the SOW. We provide runbooks and snapshot tooling.

Priya (Solutions Eng): Backup/RPO one-liners to paste?

Sam (SRE): Paste-ready bullets:
- Control plane metadata & audit logs: retention per contract (examples: 90/365).
- Hosted customer request data: short-term persisted; not covered by hosted RPO guarantees unless covered by a Dedicated backup add-on.
- Dedicated: point-in-time snapshots available; recommended cadence to approach sub-hour RPO is daily full + hourly incremental (customer config required).
- Private: customer-controlled snapshots/replication; RPO set by customer configuration and architecture.

Priya (Solutions Eng): Failover steps (concise):
1) Health checks trigger traffic routing to healthy nodes/region
2) Best-effort cache/KV prefix fallback
3) Promote warm-standby Dedicated pools if provisioned
4) DNS/edge failover for Dedicated/Private where configured
(Note: timings depend on customer topology and pre-provisioned capacity.)

Lena (Legal): Draft procurement-safe paragraph (pasteable):
"Redwood Inference operates a tiered service model. Hosted API deployments are operated for high availability and automated failover where feasible but do not include contractual RTO/RPO commitments. Dedicated capacity is provided with contractual uptime SLAs (99.9% standard, 99.95% premium) and documented recovery procedures; specific RTO/RPO values, backup cadences, and runbooks are set forth in the Service Addendum. Private deployments' recovery objectives are agreed per engagement. Data is encrypted in transit and at rest and audit logging is available. Statements are subject to the Master Services Agreement."

Alex (Sales): Nice. They also want proof of DR testing. Short attachable line we can include?

Sam (SRE): Use this: "We run quarterly DR tabletop exercises and annual live failover tests for Dedicated capacity; Private customers coordinate DR tests with their ops teams. A one-page summary of the most recent tabletop and action items can be provided on request."

Priya (Solutions Eng): I'll bundle: (1) legal paragraph; (2) backup/RPO bullets; (3) failover steps; (4) DR test line + offer the 1-page summary and anonymized 12-month availability numbers for Dedicated on request. Will cc Legal when I send.

ops-bot: DR-tabletop scheduled: 2026-06-10T16:00:00Z (reminder 7d)

Alex (Sales): Action items:
- Priya: send pasteable block + runbook excerpt to NovaSys procurement (cc Lena)
- Sam: prepare anonymized 12mo Dedicated availability metrics and the 1-page tabletop summary
- Lena: sign off final wording before we send

Priya (Solutions Eng): Sending draft to procurement now. Will post confirmation here when delivered :raised_hands:
